summary: y-prosemirror 1.3.7 deletes an ask's Yjs element from the shared document when ProseMirror's content check refuses it (sync-plugin.js:801-812); reproduced in a bun run at 2df3353c. specDepartures.spec: An editor rendering such an ask keeps every word, drawn as its literal lines with INFRA-565's drawing module, or repaired into a valid ask; the implementer chooses.
specDepartures.plan: Neither: the browser ask node type's validContent accepts what pmdoc.Validate accepts, so y-prosemirror keeps the ask as it stands; settlement marks it malformed; only an ordinary edit by a person or the asking session repairs it.
specDepartures.evidence: Drawing in the editor is written back over the ask element by the next local edit (updateYFragment) and the ask is retracted; a repair is a Yjs delete and re-insert, so repairs by every editor duplicate moved blocks and a server repair loses edits made concurrently or offline into them (offline-edits.e2e.ts:121-161). Planner's bun run: the kept ask stays editable (typing, restamp, bold, Backspace join).

specDepartures.spec: The server does not retract an ask whose text is still in the document.
specDepartures.plan: Settlement additionally marks an ask holding a second bullet list or a paragraph after its list invalid (block.invalid), keeping its row open and unchanged, where today it would index it with concatenated options.
specDepartures.evidence: The browser card reads options from the ask's last child and the question from its first (web/src/features/doc/typed-block-drawing.ts:127-170), while parseAskBlock concatenates (docs/ask_blocks.go:621-660): without the mark the card and the row disagree.

outcome.scope: A server settlement change (reconcileAskBlocks) beyond not retracting: content-rule breaks are stamped invalid like an unsupported body node.

specDepartures.spec: Pasting an unknown typed block: if any pasted word is lost, the paste keeps every word, drawn as its literal lines.
specDepartures.plan: The change is made whatever the recorded real paste shows, for every markdown parse of the live editor (paste, setMarkdown of a past version, the suggestion parser), and the live editor stops applying the paragraph-line directive refusals.
specDepartures.evidence: A throw in handlePaste skips preventDefault, handing a real paste to the browser's own contenteditable insertion outside the editor and different per browser; the suite's synthetic paste inserts nothing; the same throw fails a version view and a paste of text/::note/more. Go Render escapes those lines (pmdoc/escape_test.go:14-48).

outcome.scope: The live editor's whole markdown parse draws refused directives and keeps paragraph-line directive text, not paste of an unknown block alone.
